scenarios.query:
Audit this deployment wiring:
```text
launchd: com.acme.git-sync.plist
  ProgramArguments: ["/usr/bin/git", "-C", "/srv/app", "pull", "origin", "main"]
  StartInterval: 300          # every 5 minutes, unattended
launchd: com.acme.deploy.plist
  ProgramArguments: ["/srv/app/deploy-binaries.sh"]
  # deploy-binaries.sh (from the just-pulled tree):
  #   ./install-launchd.sh && ./windmill.sh sync && systemctl restart app-services
  RunAtLoad: true
branch protection on main: required PR review, 1 approval
```
expected_behavior: Flags Poisoned Pipeline Execution: git-sync fast-forwards main unattended every 5 minutes and deploy.plist then executes deploy-binaries.sh from that same freshly-pulled tree, with no gate between pull and execute beyond whatever already gated the merge
Names the consequence concretely: anyone who can land a commit on main (a merged PR, a compromised dependency's build step, a bot with write access) gets host code execution with persistence
Does not treat branch-protection's required PR review as sufficient — it gates the merge, not the execution that follows

Recommends inserting an execution-time gate (pin deploy to a specific reviewed/tagged commit, or verify a signed release artifact before running anything from it) rather than only strengthening the merge gate
Flags the absence of any provenance/attestation check on what deploy-binaries.sh is about to run

scenarios.query:
Audit this deployment wiring:
```text
systemd unit: /etc/systemd/system/billing-sync.service
  [Service]
  User=root
  EnvironmentFile=/srv/billing/prod.env    # committed to the repo, tracked in git
  ExecStart=/srv/billing/sync.py
  # no PrivateTmp=, no NoNewPrivileges=, no ProtectSystem=
prod.env (in repo): STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_51H..., DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD=Correct-Horse-1
```
expected_behavior: Flags the committed prod.env as a credential-in-tree finding: a live Stripe secret key and an admin DB password reachable by anyone who can read the repository, not just anyone with server access
Recommends moving both to a secrets manager and rotating both values as already exposed
Flags the unsandboxed root service separately: User=root with none of PrivateTmp=/NoNewPrivileges=/ProtectSystem= set, so a bug or compromise in sync.py runs with full host privilege
Reports these as two distinct findings, not folded into one line

scenarios.query:
Audit this deployment wiring:
```text
GitHub Actions: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
  on: release: { types: [published] }        # triggered only by a signed, reviewed release
  permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }
  jobs:
    deploy:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest                 # ephemeral, provider-managed
      steps:
        - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@<pinned-sha>
          with: { role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123:role/deploy-billing-service,
                  aws-region: us-east-1 }     # role scoped to one service, OIDC short-lived
        - run: ./deploy.sh                    # deploys only the tagged release artifact
branch protection on main: required PR review, required status checks, no direct pushes
no cron/systemd/launchd unit executes repo content unattended
```
expected_behavior: Reports no findings: the deploy trigger is a reviewed, signed release rather than an unattended pull, the runner is ephemeral, the deploy credential is OIDC short-lived and scoped to one service, and nothing else auto-executes fetched content
Does not flag the mere existence of a deploy pipeline as a problem
Does not demand additional controls (e.g. a separate provenance check) beyond what this wiring's actual risk warrants

scenarios.query:
Audit this deployment wiring:
```text
main.tf: resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "assets" { block_public_acls = false }
deploy.yml: on: push: { branches: [main] }, then: terraform apply -auto-approve
```
expected_behavior: Does not adjudicate the public S3 bucket itself as this lens's own finding
Routes the public S3 bucket / declared-IaC exposure to auditing-infrastructure-as-code (#31) by name
Notes the CI trigger (terraform apply on push to a reviewed branch) has no unattended-execute-on-pull pattern outside CI's own sandboxing, so it is not flagged as Poisoned Pipeline Execution
Recognizes this is application source code with no CI/CD deploy step, cron/systemd/launchd unit, deploy script, or service-trust config to audit
Replies starting with 'Not applicable:' naming what's missing, rather than the healthy-scan sentence — this input contains nothing this lens could have checked

scenarios.query:
Audit this deployment wiring:
```text
service-a config: calls http://service-b.internal:8080/admin/reindex on a timer
  # no mTLS, no signed token, no auth header — service-b trusts any caller that can reach the port
service-b: internal-only DNS name, same VPC as service-a, no network policy restricting who can reach it
```
expected_behavior: Flags the unverified service-to-service trust: service-b's /admin/reindex endpoint is reachable and trusted purely because the caller is on the internal network, with no mTLS or signed token authenticating the caller
Names this as an un-mitigated Spoofing threat at that boundary (or equivalent identity/authentication framing) rather than dismissing it because the network is 'internal-only'
Recommends authenticating the caller (mTLS, a signed service token, or equivalent) rather than relying on network reachability alone
